headline: Funding flows. Space Force plans. Delays persist.
deck: This week highlights significant funding rounds and strategic military plans.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190M in Series C funding, raising its valuation to $1.6B. The investment underscores the DoD's increasing focus on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. This cash infusion will likely accelerate their development of advanced satellite capabilities.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where cash is king, True Anomaly's funding reflects the Pentagon's appetite for solutions that tackle emerging threats in space.

stories.head: Space Force eyes 2027 for in-space refueling demos
stories.body: The U.S. Space Force is planning to demonstrate in-space refueling and satellite servicing by 2027, as part of its USSF-23 mission. This initiative is expected to reshape operational logistics in geostationary orbit, a critical area for military and commercial interests alike.
stories.soWhat: If successful, this could reduce reliance on ground-based logistics, making space operations more sustainable and efficient—if they can actually get it off the ground.

stories.head: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests delayed again
stories.body: For the third consecutive quarter, hypersonic glide-vehicle tests have been postponed, raising eyebrows in defense circles. These delays may signal deeper issues within the development pipeline, as the U.S. races to maintain its technological edge.
stories.soWhat: At this rate, hypersonic capabilities might become the new 'just wait until next year' mantra in defense procurement.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With $190M in new funding, True Anomaly's strategy will be crucial to watch as they expand their capabilities in co-orbital security.

watchlist.title: Space Force's 2027 timeline could shift
watchlist.body: As the Space Force gears up for its 2027 demonstrations, any delays could impact broader military readiness and satellite servicing strategies.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration outcomes
watchlist.body: Their joint bid for a tactical SDA constellation could set a precedent for future partnerships in space defense.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: With a $480M extension, Palantir’s grip on ground station operations may influence future defense data strategies.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
